entries.question: How should improvement success be judged: which metric or end state matters most?
entries.answer: Success means a human or AI can reproduce the baseline policy and decision, the exact reviewed counterfactual change, the unchanged evidence input, the baseline and counterfactual rule/route outputs, whether the route changed, which loss boundaries may be affected, why the impact remains hypothetical, what governance is required, and who retains policy authority. Replay count, route-change rate, apparent protection gain, and score differences remain evidence, never quality, truth, causality, competence, optimality, or authority.
entries.expectation_state: runtime captured first-round clarification answers and can proceed to need validation

entries.question: need validation で何が確定したか
entries.answer: The broad continuation request is reframed into the missing pre-authorization evidence contract between governed revision candidates and policy decisions; threshold-only replay and prose-only review are insufficient.

entries.question: framework self-audit で次に残る gap は何か
entries.answer: The committed variant and replay are illustrative, unverified, and not sequestered; policy-gaming resistance, contamination controls, representative cases, observed outcomes, semantic validity, and actual authorization remain unresolved.
entries.expectation_state: QIF v0.6.40 adds reviewed non-authoritative route-policy variants, deterministic same-evidence replay, explicit baseline and candidate routing, hypothetical loss-boundary impacts, aggregate assessment, and governance.
entries.mismatch_state: The committed variant and replay are illustrative, unverified, and not sequestered; policy-gaming resistance, contamination controls, representative cases, observed outcomes, semantic validity, and actual authorization remain unresolved.
entries.scale_direction: Run Council review and release v0.6.40, then implement v0.6.41 Judge Consequence and Abstention Robustness.
